record.original_question: For every graph G, is the list packing number chi*_l(G) always at most twice the list-chromatic number chi_l(G)? Equivalently, if chi_l(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits a proper coloring and chi*_l(G) is the least k such that every k-list-assignment admits k pairwise-disjoint proper colorings, must chi*_l(G) <= 2 chi_l(G) hold for all graphs G?

evidence.quote: The list-chromatic number (or choosability) chi_l(G) of a graph is the minimum integer k such that every k-list-assignment L admits an L-colouring. Given a k-list-assignment L of G we call a collection of k pairwise-disjoint L-colourings an L-packing of size k, or less specifically a list-packing. The list packing number chi*_l(G) of G is the least k such that G admits an L-packing of size k for any k-list-assignment L of G.
Problem 2.2 Is it true that chi*_l(G) <= 2chi_l(G) for every graph G?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph. A list-assignment for $G$ is a function $L$ that assigns to every vertex $v\in V(G)$ a set $L(v)$ of allowed colors; it is called a $k$-list-assignment if $|L(v)|=k$ for all $v$. An $L$-coloring of $G$ is a proper coloring $c$ of $G$ such that $c(v)\in L(v)$ for every $v$. The list-chromatic number (choosability) $\chi_\ell(G)$ is the least integer $k$ such that every $k$-list-assignment $L$ of $G$ admits an $L$-coloring.

Given a $k$-list-assignment $L$, an $L$-packing of size $k$ is a collection of $k$ proper $L$-colorings $c_1,\dots,c_k$ such that for every vertex $v$ the colors $c_1(v),\dots,c_k(v)$ are pairwise distinct (equivalently, $\{c_1(v),\dots,c_k(v)\}=L(v)$). The list packing number $\chi_\ell^\star(G)$ is the least integer $k$ such that for every $k$-list-assignment $L$ of $G$ there exists an $L$-packing of size $k$.

Determine whether the inequality
$$\chi_\ell^\star(G)\;\le\; 2\,\chi_\ell(G)$$
holds for every finite simple graph $G$.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works on list packing (Cambie–Cames van Batenburg–Davies–Kang and follow-ups) treat bounding $\chi_\ell^\star(G)$ in terms of $\chi_\ell(G)$ as an open direction; only partial results (e.g., the fractional analogue, bounded-degree and degeneracy bounds $\chi_\ell^\star\le 2\Delta$ or $2d$, and special graph classes) are known. No proof or counterexample to the general inequality $\chi_\ell^\star(G)\le 2\chi_\ell(G)$ appears in the literature retrieved.

status_evidence.title: List packing number of bounded degree graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Bounds the list packing number for bounded-degree graphs; the question of bounding χ*_ℓ by a function of χ_ℓ remains a driving open problem.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial bounds (in terms of degree/degeneracy) are known.

status_evidence.title: Fractional List Packing for Layered Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: States a fractional List Packing Conjecture: there exists C>0 such that the fractional list packing number is at most C·χ_ℓ(G).
status_evidence.claim: The relationship between χ*_ℓ and χ_ℓ is studied via fractional relaxations and remains conjectural.

status_evidence.title: A Short Proof that the List Packing Number of any Graph is Well Defined
status_evidence.snippet: Shows χ*_ℓ(G) is finite for every graph but does not establish the 2χ_ℓ bound.
status_evidence.claim: Finiteness is known; the 2χ_ℓ bound is not established.
